mcqs.question: What did Justice Dipak Misra receive as part of the Kalinga Ratna Award from Sarala Sahitya Sansad, Cuttack?
options: A silver idol of Goddess Saraswati and a citation
A bronze idol of Goddess Saraswati and a citation
A silver idol of Goddess Lakshmi and a citation
A gold idol of Goddess Saraswati and a citation
mcqs.explanation: Justice Dipak Misra received a silver idol of Goddess Saraswati and a citation with the Kalinga Ratna Award. The tempting alternative of a bronze idol is incorrect because the award included a silver idol.

mcqs.question: Which pairing is correct regarding the Arthur M. Bueche Award and the US National Academy of Engineering?
options: The award was instituted in 1982–83, and NAE was established in 1964
The award was instituted in 1985–86, and NAE was established in 1969
The award was instituted in 1982–83, and NAE was established in 1974
The award was instituted in 1992–93, and NAE was established in 1964
mcqs.explanation: The Arthur M. Bueche Award was instituted in 1982–83, while the National Academy of Engineering was established in 1964. The other options alter one or both of these dates.

mcqs.question: Who was the second runner-up of Miss World 2026, and who crowned the winner?
options: Tanusia Shetty and Opal Suchata Chuangsri
Elizabeth Rains and Opal Suchata Chuangsri
Tanusia Shetty and Zohery Mola
Elizabeth Rains and Tanusia Shetty
mcqs.explanation: Tanusia Shetty of Malaysia was the second runner-up, and Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand, Miss World 2025, crowned the winner. Elizabeth Rains was the first runner-up, not the second runner-up.

mcqs.keyword: Indian Miss World winners and years
mcqs.question:
Match the Indian Miss World winners in List-I with their winning years in List-II.

List-I
(a) Reita Faria
(b) Aishwarya Rai
(c) Diana Hayden
(d) Yukta Mookhey

List-II
(i) 1997
(ii) 1966
(iii) 1999
(iv) 1994
options: a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i
a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Reita Faria–1966, Aishwarya Rai–1994, Diana Hayden–1997 and Yukta Mookhey–1999. The other codes interchange the years of these Indian Miss World winners.

mcqs.keyword: Miss World background and Dominican Republic
mcqs.question:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct details in List-II.

List-I
(a) Priyanka Chopra
(b) Manushi Chhillar
(c) Miss World
(d) Capital of the Dominican Republic

List-II
(i) Santo Domingo
(ii) 2000
(iii) 1951; founded by Eric Morley
(iv) 2017
options: a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i
a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
mcqs.explanation: Priyanka Chopra won in 2000, Manushi Chhillar won in 2017, Miss World began in 1951 and was founded by Eric Morley, and Santo Domingo is the capital of the Dominican Republic. The alternative codes mismatch these years, the founding detail or the capital.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following countries are stated to have won the most Miss World titles, with six titles each?

1. India
2. Venezuela
3. United Kingdom
4. Jamaica
options: Only one
Only two
Only three
All four
mcqs.explanation: India and Venezuela are each credited with six Miss World titles, so exactly two countries in the list have that total. The United Kingdom has five titles and Jamaica has four.

mcqs.question: The Global Cooling Pledge, launched at COP28 in Dubai in 2023, was notable as what kind of commitment?
options: The first global commitment focused on cooling
The first global commitment focused on ocean conservation
The first global commitment focused on agricultural science
The first global commitment focused on book publishing
mcqs.explanation: The Global Cooling Pledge was the first global commitment focused on cooling and was associated with COP28 in Dubai in 2023. The other options refer to areas not identified with this pledge.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Sarah Peluse is an Assistant Professor at Stanford University.
Statement B: Her work also includes combinatorial geometry and group theory.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is false because Sarah Peluse is an Associate Professor, not an Assistant Professor. Statement B is true because her work also includes combinatorial geometry and group theory.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): CAST stands for the Council for Agricultural Science and Technology, and Dr. Karim Maredia has been at Michigan State University since 1989.
Reason (R): The Library of Congress was established in 1800.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is false because CAST does stand for the Council for Agricultural Science and Technology, but the stated association with Michigan State University since 1989 is separate from the assertion as framed. Reason R is true because the Library of Congress was established in 1800.

mcqs.question: Who is identified as the Father of India's Green Revolution in the context of the Borlaug CAST Award?
options: M. S. Swaminathan
Norman Borlaug
Karim Maredia
Sethuraman Panchanathan
mcqs.explanation: M. S. Swaminathan is identified as the Father of India's Green Revolution. Norman Borlaug is associated with the Nobel Peace Prize and the Borlaug name, but he is not the person identified by this title in the fact.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the American Geophysical Union is incorrect?
options: AGU was established in 1919.
AGU is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
AGU was established in 1929.
AGU is an organisation associated with the 2026 awards recognising Roxy Mathew Koll and Neelima Satyam.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that AGU was established in 1929; the correct year is 1919. AGU is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and its 2026 awards included recognition of Roxy Mathew Koll and Neelima Satyam.

mcqs.question: Which organisation, established in 1989 in New York City, runs the National Book Awards?
options: National Book Foundation
US National Academy of Engineering
National Mathematics Day Committee
American Geophysical Union
mcqs.explanation: The National Book Foundation was established in 1989 in New York City and runs the National Book Awards. The other organisations are associated with engineering, mathematics or geophysical science rather than the National Book Awards.
